mainTopic: תדיר versus מקודש: tomorrow's תמיד or today's מוספין, and the six checked lambs of the לשכת הטלאים
overview: The גמרא is trying to answer the question of רבי חייא בר אבין: if the Temple has only enough animals for today's מוספין or for tomorrow's תמיד, which one comes first? Tomorrow's תמיד is תדיר (more frequent), and today's מוספין are מקודש (their day has already arrived). רב חסדא tries to prove from the משנה that the two are equal, because it says the תמידין and מוספין do not hold each other back. אביי rejects this: the משנה may be talking only about the order, and the ברייתא that says nothing comes before the morning תמיד describes only the ideal way. Next the גמרא tries a משנה in ערכין that says to keep at least six checked lambs for שבת and the two days of ראש השנה, which seems to show that the תמידין come first. This proof is also rejected. The six lambs are only the ones checked four days before slaughter, following בן בג בג, who learns this four-day check from the קרבן פסח. Finally רבינא asks רב אשי why the count is six and not seven, since Tuesday morning's lamb also needs checking. רב אשי answers that by that logic it would be eight, and רבינא explains that the count starts after Friday afternoon's offering, so his question about seven still stands as the amud ends.

steps.title: So the משנה must be talking about a shortage of animals
steps.stepSummary: Since the case of 'having enough animals' was already ruled out, the משנה must be about a case where there are not enough animals for both offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that the משנה is talking about a case where he does not have enough animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ruling out the first way of reading the משנה and decides it must be about a shortage of animals. This sets up the next question: which day's offerings is it talking about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא showed that 'they do not hold each other back' cannot be about having enough animals and only the order, because a ברייתא says nothing may come before the morning תמיד. So the only option left is a case where there are not enough animals for both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
He does not have (enough animals)
Rather; introduces the only remaining option

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that he does not have [enough]!
phrases.notes: He means not enough animals in the Temple treasury for both the תמיד and the מוספין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the elimination of the 'he has enough animals' reading begun just before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is about a shortage of animals.

steps.title: It cannot mean today's תמיד, because the תמיד would clearly win
steps.stepSummary: If the shortage were between today's תמיד and today's מוספין, the תמיד would obviously come first, so the משנה could not call them equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it means today's offerings, why would they not hold each other back? The תמיד is both frequent and sanctified, and the frequent one wins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible reading, that the משנה is about today's תמיד, and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today's תמיד and today's מוספין are both מקודש, because their day has come. But the תמיד is also תדיר, more frequent, and the rule is תדיר comes first. So the תמיד should win, and the משנה could not say the two are equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Of that same day
Frequent; an offering brought more often
Sanctified; here, its day has already arrived
The more frequent one takes precedence

steps.confusionAlert: Here the תמיד has both qualities, תדיר and מקודש, so it clearly wins. The real question of רבי חייא בר אבין is about tomorrow's תמיד, which is only תדיר, against today's מוספין, which are only מקודש.

phrases.english: And if [it means the תמיד] of that day, why?
phrases.notes: Why would the משנה say they don't hold each other back?

phrases.english: Frequent and sanctified: the frequent one takes precedence!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled on a shortage case, it rules out the reading that the shortage is about today's תמיד.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as being about today's תמיד against today's מוספין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Today's תמיד is both תדיר and מקודש, so by the rule תדיר עדיף it must come first, which contradicts the משנה's claim that neither holds the other back.

steps.title: So it must mean tomorrow's תמיד, proving the two are equal
steps.stepSummary: The only reading left is today's מוספין against tomorrow's תמיד. Since the משנה says neither holds the other back, they must be equal, which answers the question of רבי חייא בר אבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not about tomorrow's תמיד? And the משנה teaches that they do not hold each other back. This shows they are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out the other readings, רב חסדא concludes the משנה is about tomorrow's תמיד, and uses it to prove the two kinds of offerings are equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tomorrow's תמיד is תדיר but its day has not come yet. Today's מוספין are מקודש but less frequent. Since the משנה lets either go first, neither quality beats the other, and he may choose either one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not; introduces the remaining reading as a proof
Of tomorrow
They do not hold each other back
Evidently; this shows that
They are equal to each other

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, it would fully answer the question of תדיר against מקודש: neither one takes precedence.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not [the תמיד] of tomorrow,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי אֵין מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: and it teaches: they do not hold each other back,
evidently, they are equal to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After eliminating today's תמיד, it settles on tomorrow's תמיד and draws the proof.
steps.raayaObject: The question of רבי חייא בר אבין: tomorrow's תמיד (תדיר) against today's מוספין (מקודש)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: the תמידין and מוספין do not hold each other back

steps.title: אביי: the משנה is about order, and the ברייתא is only the ideal
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The משנה can be about having enough animals and only about which goes first. The ברייתא saying nothing comes before the morning תמיד is only the ideal way, not a strict requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, it is a case where they have enough animals, and the question is about which goes first. And as for what bothered you, that nothing may come before the morning תמיד, that is just the ideal מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down the proof by bringing back the first reading that רב חסדא had thrown out, and explaining away the ברייתא that seemed to rule it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא had ruled out the 'enough animals' reading because of the ברייתא. אביי says the ברייתא only describes the best way to do it. So the משנה can mean that offering the מוספין before the תמיד does not ruin anything after the fact, and it tells us nothing about a shortage case.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (bringing back an earlier option)
Where they have (enough animals)
And it is about which goes first
Merely the ideal מצוה, not a requirement that holds things back

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה fails. אביי reads it as being about order, and the rule that the morning תמיד comes first is only the ideal way. So the גמרא tries a new source in step 5.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Actually, it is where they have [enough], and it is about going first.
And as for what is difficult for you,
that nothing should come before [the morning תמיד],
it is merely the ideal מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3 by bringing back the reading that step 1 had ruled out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'enough animals' reading was ruled out too quickly. The ברייתא only states the ideal way, so the משנה can be about order.

steps.title: A new attempt: six checked lambs kept ready
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from ערכין: the Temple always keeps at least six checked lambs in the לשכת הטלאים, enough for שבת and the two days of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: they never keep fewer than six inspected lambs in the Chamber of the Lambs, enough for שבת and the two festival days of ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer the question of רבי חייא בר אבין by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the source; the proof drawn from it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets a minimum stock of six lambs that are already checked for blemishes, enough to cover the תמיד for three days in a row, such as when שבת is next to the two days of ראש השנה. The exact number will become the basis for the next proof.

keyTerms.meaning: They never go below; a minimum is kept
Lambs
Inspected and found free of blemishes
The Chamber of the Lambs in the Temple
Festival days

phrases.english: Come and hear:
They do not keep fewer than six lambs
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in ערכין 13a.

phrases.english: that are inspected, in the Chamber of the Lambs,
enough for שבת

phrases.aramaic: וְלִשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: and for the two festival days of ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשִּׁשָּׁה טְלָאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי rejected the first proof, the גמרא starts a new attempt from a different source.
steps.raayaObject: The question of רבי חייא בר אבין: תדיר against מקודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in ערכין 13a about keeping six inspected lambs ready

steps.title: What case is the six-lamb משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation the משנה describes. It rules out the case where there are enough animals for both the תמידין and the מוספין, because those days need many more than six lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say the Temple has enough for all the daily and additional offerings, then many lambs would be needed, not just six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which situation the ערכין משנה is describing. It knocks out the first option right away, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Over שבת and two days of ראש השנה, the תמידין and מוספין together need far more than six lambs. So if the Temple had enough for everything, six would not be the right number. That pushes us toward the case of a shortage.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
If you say..., the first possible option
A lot, many

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the ערכין משנה from the last step, the one that says to keep at least six checked lambs.

phrases.english: If we say that he has enough for the daily offerings and the additional offerings,
they are many!
phrases.notes: Those three days need about 22 lambs in total once you count every תמיד and every מוסף, so six is far too few.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case of the ערכין משנה brought in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the משנה describing a case with enough animals or a case with a shortage?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not the case of having enough, since that would need many more than six lambs

steps.title: So it must be a shortage, and the daily offerings come first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must be about a shortage of animals. Since the six lambs are kept for the תמידין of all three days, this proves that tomorrow's תמיד takes priority over today's מוספין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it a case where he does not have enough? Learn from this that the daily offerings take priority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה must describe a shortage. From that it draws a proof that the תמידין come first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only six lambs, the Temple saves them for the תמידין of all three days instead of using them for שבת's מוסף. That means tomorrow's תמיד beats today's מוסף, which answers the earlier question in favor of the תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? The only option left
Learn from this, a proof is drawn
Take priority, are preferred

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that he does not have enough,
and learn from this that the daily offerings take priority!
phrases.notes: He means tomorrow's תמיד comes before today's מוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו דְּלֵית לֵיהּ, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruled-out option from step 6 to reach the shortage case and draw a proof
steps.raayaObject: Tomorrow's תמיד takes priority over today's מוספין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ערכין משנה that requires only six checked lambs for שבת and two days of ראש השנה

steps.title: No, the six lambs are only the ones checked four days ahead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה can be about having enough animals, and it means that at least six lambs must be checked four days before slaughter. This follows בן בג בג.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really he has enough, and this is what the משנה means: we keep no fewer than six lambs that were checked in the lamb chamber four days before slaughter. Whose view is this? בן בג בג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers a new way to read the six-lamb rule, so it no longer needs a shortage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six lambs are not all the Temple has. They are the lambs that must be checked four days before they are slaughtered, which is needed only for the תמיד. Other lambs for the מוספין can be there too, so the משנה tells us nothing about which offering comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually, going back to the first option
Checked and found to have no blemish
Whose opinion is this?

steps.confusionAlert: The six lambs are not the Temple's whole supply. They are only the lambs already checked for the תמיד; more lambs can be on hand for the מוספין.

phrases.english: No, actually it is a case where he has enough,
and this is what it is saying:
one does not have fewer than six lambs
that are checked in the Chamber of the Lambs
four days before slaughter,
And whose view is this? It is בן בג בג's.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם דְּאִית לֵיהּ, וְהָכִי קָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7 by going back to the 'enough animals' case that step 6 ruled out
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that תמידין take priority
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed six was the total number of lambs; it is really the minimum number of lambs checked four days in advance

steps.title: בן בג בג's source for checking the תמיד four days ahead
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that בן בג בג learns the four-day check for the תמיד from the קרבן פסח, using a shared word about 'guarding'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught: בן בג בג says, from where do we know the תמיד must be checked four days before slaughter? The verse says 'You shall guard to offer to Me in its time,' and elsewhere it says 'It shall be guarded for you until the fourteenth day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim that the six-lamb משנה follows בן בג בג. It quotes his source for checking the תמיד four days ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the root שמר, 'guard'. The פסח lamb was taken on the tenth and guarded until the fourteenth, which is four days. בן בג בג applies that four-day guarding to the תמיד too.

keyTerms.meaning: Checking an animal for blemishes
The verse teaches
Elsewhere, in another place in the תורה
Guarding, keeping watch

steps.whatToRemember: The six-lamb משנה does not prove that tomorrow's תמיד comes first. It only teaches the minimum number of lambs checked four days ahead, following בן בג בג, who learns this from the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: As it is taught: בן בג בג says:
From where do we know that the daily offering needs checking
four days before slaughter?
The verse teaches:
"You shall guard to offer to Me in its time,"
and elsewhere it says:
"And it shall be guarded for you
until the fourteenth day."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:6, about the פסח lamb. It was taken on the tenth, so it was guarded for four days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 8's claim that the משנה follows בן בג בג
steps.raayaObject: That there is a view requiring the תמיד to be checked four days before slaughter
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of בן בג בג comparing the 'guarding' of the תמיד to the 'guarding' of the קרבן פסח

steps.title: The four-day check carries over from the קרבן פסח to the תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its comparison: the תמיד needs a four-day check before slaughter, just like the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there (the קרבן פסח) it needs to be checked four days before slaughter, so too here (the תמיד) it needs to be checked four days before slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the ברייתא from the last step. It states the result of the comparison: the תמיד, like the קרבן פסח, must be checked four days before it is slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared word about 'guarding' links the two קרבנות, so the rule moves from the פסח to the תמיד. This supports the reading from step 8: the משנה's six lambs means six lambs that were already checked four days early, following בן בג בג.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there... so too here: the standard way of carrying a rule from one case to another
Requires inspection, checking the animal for blemishes
Before slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: According to בן בג בג, the תמיד lamb must be checked four days before slaughter. He learns this from the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: Just as there, it requires inspection
phrases.notes: 'There' means the קרבן פסח, which was set aside on the tenth of the month and slaughtered on the fourteenth.

phrases.english: four days before slaughter,
so too here, it requires inspection
four days before slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן טָעוּן בִּיקּוּר אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's גזרה שוה that began in step 9
steps.raayaObject: That the תמיד needs a four-day check before slaughter
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of בן בג בג, using a גזרה שוה from the קרבן פסח

steps.title: רבינא asks why the count is six and not seven
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the number six in the משנה: Tuesday morning's תמיד also needs a lamb checked ahead of time, so there should be seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: These six? They should be seven, because there is also the lamb for the morning of the third day of the week!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the משנה's number. רבינא says six lambs is not enough. Seven are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture שבת followed by two days of ראש השנה, on Sunday and Monday. Those three days need six lambs, one in the morning and one in the afternoon each day. But the lamb for Tuesday morning also cannot be checked on those days, so it must be prepared beforehand too, which makes seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven
Morning: here, the morning תמיד
The third day of the week, which is Tuesday

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
These six? They are seven,
phrases.notes: He is asking about the six checked lambs from the משנה in ערכין (step 5).

phrases.english: for there is the one for the morning of the third day of the week!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the number in the משנה from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's number of six checked lambs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tuesday morning's lamb also falls in the period when checking cannot be done, so it should be counted, making seven

steps.title: רב אשי replies that by that logic it should be eight
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes back: if you count Tuesday morning, you should also count Friday afternoon's תמיד, which would make eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, they should be eight, because there is also the lamb for the afternoon of Friday!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא with a counter-question. If we start counting extra lambs, Friday afternoon's lamb should be counted too, so the total would be eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'your logic proves too much' move. If we count a lamb outside the three days, like Tuesday morning's, then Friday afternoon's lamb should count too, and the משנה should say eight, not seven. That forces רבינא to explain what point in time the משנה is counting from.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the other person's logic back on him
Eight
Afternoon: here, the afternoon תמיד
The eve of שבת, which is Friday

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, they are eight,
for there is the one for the afternoon of Shabbat eve!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-challenge to רבינא's question in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's way of counting the lambs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If extra lambs beyond the three days count, Friday afternoon's should count as well, which gives eight and not seven

steps.title: The count starts after Friday afternoon's offering
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that Friday afternoon's lamb is no problem, because the משנה counts the lambs after that offering has already been brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult, because the משנה speaks of the time after he has already brought the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אשי's counter-question. Friday afternoon's lamb is not counted because the משנה counts what must be left after it has already been offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once Friday afternoon's lamb has been brought, it is no longer waiting in the chamber, so it drops out of the count. Tuesday morning's lamb, though, is still in the future. So רבינא's original question, why six and not seven, still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not difficult: introduces an answer to a challenge
After
He brought the offering

phrases.english: That is not difficult,
phrases.notes: This is רבינא speaking again, answering רב אשי's 'eight' point.

phrases.english: for it is speaking of after he has sacrificed.
phrases.notes: He means after the Friday afternoon תמיד was already offered. Only then must six lambs be left.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, דִּלְבָתַר דְּאַקְרֵיב קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's counter-challenge from step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sets the point in time the משנה is counting from
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Friday afternoon's lamb should be in the count too, making eight
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה counts after Friday afternoon's offering, so that lamb is excluded. Tuesday morning's lamb is still a question.
